headline: Long-read pangenomes resolve mobile and repetitive variation in human genomes
label: Human Pangenome Variant Discovery
summary: Long-read pangenome assemblies now allow repetitive, mobile, and structural variation to be cataloged and linked to traits in population-scale studies.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that long-read pangenome assemblies resolve repetitive and mobile sequence. The HPRC-based LINE-1 study uses 47 assemblies to catalog intact alleles and population dynamics. A pangenome graph approach to NUMT detection reports 2.52-fold better sensitivity, yielding 774 fixed and 280 polymorphic events. ImputeSV, built on a long-read-derived SV reference panel, imputes structural variants from SNPs, enabling GWAS of SVs across 2,624 UK Biobank traits. Complementary work addresses read-level ambiguity: ParaDISM refines short-read alignments in highly homologous regions, and ERVmancer quantifies endogenous retrovirus expression. PfPan extends pangenome SV discovery to Plasmodium falciparum. Not every item shares this thread, but the new element is the move from assembly content toward trait-level association.
